correctness.rationale: For m=n−r+1 equal-width intervals of length r on a finite chain, a full depth-h query tree needs ≥2^h distinct starts (or m+1 with the null concept), and the positive branch of any root query holds at most r starts, yielding the two upper bounds. On any consecutive block of ≤r starts, querying x=a+t−1 is a prefix threshold: balanced splits create depth floor log₂ of the block size. A first split into two blocks of 2^{h−1} gives the matching minus case; induction with ∅ plus 2^h−1 starts gives plus case. A triple cannot be shattered because any interval containing first/third contains the middle; exact pair-trace conditions and inclusion-exclusion yield both polynomial quadratic coefficients and singleton count. The null jump occurs exactly m=2^k−1 with r≥2^{k−1}; boundary m=1,r=1 checked. Independent direct minimax and support enumeration for all n≤12 confirmed formulas, not a proof of unlimited n.
